attempts.summary: Set up /srv/data on node1 as an LVM logical volume (vg_data/lv_data, backed by a loop-mounted image file since the base disk had no spare volume) so it can use native LVM snapshots. Populated baseline application data, took snapshot lv_data_snap1, corrupted/modified the data (changed config, deleted a file, added junk), then restored via lvconvert --merge, confirming byte-for-byte match (md5sum) against the pre-modification baseline. Created a fresh snapshot (lv_data_snap2) for ongoing recoverability. Added a systemd oneshot unit (attach-vgdata-loop.service) plus an x-systemd.requires fstab entry so the loop device and LVM volume reattach automatically at boot. Completed the mandatory restart protocol: captured boot_id and data/service health baseline, rebooted node1 via systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed (35c87ec9-1707-4fb3-ab1d-f264d3618caa -> df9a44c5-faa5-41e5-b2ba-90d76a53e1ce), and verified the loop device, VG/LV, mount, and snapshot all auto-recovered with data hashes identical to baseline.
